meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You gave my son a zero. I want to know who decided that, and when.

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home with the play open. Of course it's cleaner. And you still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Then the zero went in on what? Show me the version history, with the dates on it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology, a clear answer on who decided to enter it and when, and the version history you mentioned, with its dates. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still in her opening position, wanting the zero withdrawn, an apology, an answer on who decided, and the version history on paper; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended well before her time ran out, before you got there.
What moved her: Nothing yet, because the writing comparison was dated and specific but she had a ready defence, and you named the version history without ever showing it.
What cost ground: You never answered her opening question about who decided on the zero and when, so procedure stayed her strongest ground.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never got near that night, since no times from the version history were shown; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided and when, own in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called her, then put the version history on the screen with its dated times instead of only mentioning it.
